A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PERSIST research work. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching renamed configurations and relocated material.

before.justification: V1 reports original FVD measurements, a 28-participant human study, and generated-world demonstrations in Section 6 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains original human-study results and reports revised quantitative evaluations, component ablations, stability measurements, and inference-speed experiments.

M1.justification: The full PERSIST architecture, objectives, projection mechanism, exposure-bias mitigation, and Algorithms 1–2 remain unchanged. PERSIST-XL is renamed PERSIST; component ablations and reduced denoising-step settings are experimental variants.

E1.justification: Both versions cover procedural voxel-world simulation using Craftium/Luanti and retain Minecraft/MineDojo evaluations in the human study. V2 aligns quantitative baselines with the existing Craftium data; the additional ablations and horizon measurements do not introduce a new domain or task.

E2.justification: Oasis and WorldMem remain the external baselines. V2 Table 1 adds No-3D-Upscale and Camera-GT as explicit comparison variants alongside the retained PERSIST configurations, providing a limited expansion of the comparator lineup.

E3.justification: V2 replaces the released, Minecraft-trained quantitative baselines with models trained on shared data using the same VAEs and rectified-flow formulation. Evaluation changes from 148 trajectories of 192 frames to 168 trajectories with 200/400/600-frame measurements; WorldMem's quantitative warm-start changes from 600 to 400 frames. Per-timestep FID and controlled timing and denoising-step experiments are added. The original human-study protocol is retained.

E4.justification: Beyond the retained resolution and initial-state comparisons, v2 adds upscaling and camera ablations, per-timestep stability analysis, a camera-related physical-failure example, and inference speed–quality analysis. Appendix B also adds a comparison of human ratings across ground-truth domains. The existing 2,000-step artifact-and-recovery example is retained, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Human-rating uncertainty terms remain unchanged. Neither version supplies new repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence-interval procedures, or formal significance tests; the added domain-rating comparison reports an outcome without introducing an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: The original single-horizon FVD results are replaced under revised conditions: PERSIST-XL's 181 becomes PERSIST results of 129/141/148 at 200/400/600 frames. WorldMem reports 358 only at 200 frames, with longer-horizon entries absent. New results include ablation scores, FID curves, and a fast PERSIST-S configuration reporting 886 ms per frame and FVD 207/230/244. These are not same-setting performance gains over v1. Human-study scores remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The formal environment definition, flow-matching objective, sampling equations, and mathematical model specification are retained. No theorem, proof, substantive derivation, or formal assumption is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: persistent 3D state improves spatial memory and generation consistency while enabling image-based initialization, explicit world editing, and off-screen dynamics. The additional experiments support these existing contributions.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations linking upscaling to depth resolution and alignment, and learned cameras to physical consistency that FVD can miss. It explains the initial FID penalty and explicitly acknowledges that inference is not real time. Existing limitations concerning 3D supervision, exposure bias, and finite spatial memory remain.

D1.justification: Appendix D newly discloses key-value caching, timing conditions using one A100 and batch size 1, component runtimes, and the reduced-step configuration. Appendix B adds participant-background information. Existing architecture tables, training hardware and durations, losses, and default sampling hyperparameters are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds Heusel et al. (2017) for FID and removes the introductory characterization of frontier models as having one-minute visual memory. The substantive positioning against pixel-history retrieval, static 3D environments, and neural rendering remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 reorganizes Section 6.1 into explicit ablation, quantitative, stability, human-study, and efficiency discussions, and separates quantitative and human-study methodology in Appendix B. It renames the XL configuration, makes local language edits, and adds acknowledgments and a conference footer. Most foundational and methodological prose remains intact.

P2.justification: The combined results table becomes separate FVD and human-rating tables. V2 adds the FID plot, timing tables, and camera-failure figure, and expands the off-screen dynamics illustration. It also combines four full-page heatmaps into one multipanel figure, consolidates hyperparameter tables, and places both inference algorithms together, substantially revising the visual organization.

improvement.justification: V2 substantially strengthens the empirical foundation by replacing v1's quantitative comparisons across different training and evaluation domains with shared-data, shared-VAE comparisons. Component ablations and stability measurements better test the central explanation, while timing results clarify practical feasibility. The retained human study still spans different domains, and WorldMem lacks longer-horizon FVD entries, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial improvement in experimental support and transparency.
